content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today's world." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.

modelEssay.title: Digital Literacy and Skills
modelEssay.content:
There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today's world. In the digital age, being proficient in digital skills is no longer a luxury but a necessity. The rapid advancement of technology has made digital literacy a fundamental requirement for personal and professional success.

For instance, in the workplace, digital skills enable employees to work more efficiently and effectively. They can use software to manage tasks, collaborate with colleagues remotely, and analyze data to make informed decisions. Moreover, digital literacy is essential for students who need to access online resources, participate in virtual classes, and conduct research using digital tools. Personal experiences also underscore the significance of digital skills. I remember struggling with basic computer operations when I first started college, but as I honed my digital skills, I found myself more capable and confident in my academic and extracurricular activities.

In conclusion, digital literacy and skills are indispensable in our increasingly digital world. They not only enhance our ability to navigate the digital landscape but also empower us to contribute meaningfully to society.

transcript.text: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.speaker: F

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 玛格丽特，我们这样来回修改已经快一年了。

transcript.text: Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your client or not?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你确定要为你的客户达成赞助协议吗？

transcript.text: I ask this because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我这样问是因为，坦白说，我这边有些人已经快失去耐心了。

transcript.text: I understand your concerns, but as I'm sure you understand, we hold our client's best interests to be of the utmost concern.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我理解你的担忧，但我相信你也明白，我们始终将客户的最大利益放在首位。

transcript.text: We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 因此，我们会仔细审查所有合同的细节。

transcript.text: Rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 请放心，我们都感激贵公司的耐心。

transcript.text: Okay, fine.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 好吧，好的。

transcript.text: So, what changes do you wish to make?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么，你希望做哪些改动？

transcript.text: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East, that's all.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 基本上，我们希望新协议排除中东地区，仅此而已。

transcript.text: The Middle East, why?
transcript.speaker: M

transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我的客户有其他几个来自中东公司的潜在营销交易。

transcript.translation: 那些提议，如果实现的话，将仅在中东地区独家使用我客户的形象。

transcript.text: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地理上不重叠。

transcript.text: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?

transcript.text: Well, that should be okay then.

transcript.translation: 那么，这应该没问题。

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 只要产品与我们的食品和饮料市场有很大不同，就不会有利益冲突。

transcript.text: I don't foresee any problem, though.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过，我认为不会有问题。

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Next, we have a special science-related news story.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 接下来，我们有一则特别的与科学相关的新闻报道。

transcript.text: Why?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 为什么？

transcript.text: What's the big event?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 什么重大事件？

transcript.text: Is there an eclipse happening soon?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 很快会有日食或月食发生吗？

transcript.text: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 今晚，地球将接近奥本海默彗星。

transcript.text: It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这是我们的星球在100多年来最接近这种现象的一次。

transcript.text: For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 因此，预计今晚将有数千人仰望天空，以观看这个壮观的天体。

transcript.text: How far away is this comet?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这颗彗星有多远？

transcript.text: Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们能用肉眼看到它吗？

transcript.text: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 奥本海默彗星仍然在数百万英里之外，在我们星系的边缘。

transcript.text: But, nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但是，尽管如此，这是一个相对较近的距离，足够近，人们可以通过望远镜详细观测。

transcript.text: People will only see a blur without one.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没有望远镜，人们只能看到一个模糊的影像。

transcript.text: However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 然而，这并不意味着需要专业设备。

transcript.text: Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 即使是最普通的望远镜也应该有助于人们观测和惊叹这个飞行物。

transcript.text: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们的许多观众会想知道他们如何也能参与这次千载难逢的事件。

transcript.text: Where will this comet be in the sky?

transcript.text: How can people find it?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 人们如何找到它？

transcript.text: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 彗星将在几乎正北方向，赤道上方60度处。

transcript.text: However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky, and scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 然而，找到彗星确实非常棘手，这里的科学家告诉我有很多手机应用程序可以方便这个。

transcript.text: How fantastic!

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
transcript.translation: 饮食指南构成了世界各地营养建议和法规的基础。

transcript.text: While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate.
transcript.translation: 尽管对大多数现有指南存在强烈的科学共识，但一个问题最近引发了争论。

transcript.text: Should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
transcript.translation: 应该警告消费者避免超加工食品吗？

transcript.text: Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems.
transcript.translation: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文概述了支持和反对使用超加工食品概念来帮助超越传统食品分类系统制定饮食指南的论据。

transcript.text: The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of Sao Paulo and Arne Ostrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate, August 14th, during Nutrition 2024 Live Online.
transcript.translation: 作者，圣保罗大学的卡洛斯·蒙泰罗和诺和诺德基金会的阿恩·奥斯特鲁普，将在8月14日的Nutrition 2024 Live Online期间通过直播虚拟辩论讨论这个问题。

transcript.text: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
transcript.translation: 辩论围绕蒙泰罗及其同事开发的一个系统展开，该系统根据食品的工业加工程度对食品进行分类，从未加工到超加工。

transcript.text: The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
transcript.translation: 该系统将超加工食品定义为那些使用一系列工艺制成的食品，这些工艺从食品中提取物质并用化学物质改变它们，以配方成最终产品。

transcript.text: Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient.
transcript.translation: 超加工食品的特征是设计得廉价、美味和方便。

transcript.text: Examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
transcript.translation: 例子包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、即热产品以及重组肉制品。

transcript.text: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods, which are often high in salt, sugar, and fat, with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet.
transcript.translation: 研究已将超加工食品的消费与体重增加和慢性病风险增加联系起来，这些食品通常盐、糖和脂肪含量高，即使在对饮食中盐、糖和脂肪的量进行调整后也是如此。

transcript.text: While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
transcript.translation: 尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未完全理解，但蒙泰罗认为，现有证据足以证明在饮食建议和政府政策中劝阻超加工食品的消费是合理的。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 段落2。

transcript.text: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
transcript.translation: 信不信由你，人类创造力受益于约束。

transcript.text: According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
transcript.translation: 心理学家表示，当你可利用的资源更少时，你实际上开始以不同方式看待世界。

transcript.text: With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
transcript.translation: 有了约束，你将心理能量投入到更足智多谋的行动中。

transcript.text: When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
transcript.translation: 当面临挑战时，你会找出新的方法来变得更好。

transcript.text: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
transcript.translation: 最成功的创意人士知道，约束给予他们的心灵跳得更高的动力。

transcript.text: People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do.
transcript.translation: 发明新产品的人不会受限于他们没有或做不到的事情。

transcript.text: They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
transcript.translation: 他们利用自己的局限来更进一步地推动自己。

transcript.text: Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use.
transcript.translation: 许多产品和服务的创造是因为创始人在他们使用的东西中看到了局限性。

transcript.text: They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
transcript.translation: 他们基于当时对他们不起作用的东西创造了创新。

transcript.text: Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation.
transcript.translation: 创新是创意人士对局限性的回应。

transcript.text: In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways.
transcript.translation: 在2015年的一项研究中，该研究考察了思考稀缺或丰富如何影响人们创造性地使用资源的方式，伊利诺伊大学的Ravi Mehta和约翰霍普金斯大学的Meng Zhu发现，人们根本就没有动力以新颖的方式使用他们可用的资源。

transcript.text: When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
transcript.translation: 当人们面临稀缺时，他们给自己自由以不那么传统的方式使用资源，因为他们不得不这样做。

transcript.text: Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
transcript.translation: 障碍可以拓宽你的感知并打开你的思维过程。

transcript.text: Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
transcript.translation: 持续的约束帮助你提高连接不相关想法和概念的能力。

transcript.text: Marissa Meyer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome.
transcript.translation: 谷歌前搜索产品和用户体验副总裁Marissa Meyer曾在彭博社的一篇文章中写道，约束塑造和聚焦问题，并提供清晰的挑战来克服。

transcript.text: Creativity thrives best when constrained.
transcript.translation: 创造力在约束下蓬勃发展得最好。

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音1.

transcript.text: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
transcript.translation: 不同的人使用不同的策略来管理冲突。

transcript.text: These strategies are learned in childhood.
transcript.translation: 这些策略是在童年时期学会的。

transcript.text: Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
transcript.translation: 通常，我们并不意识到自己在冲突情境中是如何行动的。

transcript.text: We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
transcript.translation: 我们只是做那些看起来自然而然的事情。

transcript.text: But, we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
transcript.translation: 但是，我们确实有个人策略，而且因为它是学来的，我们总是可以通过学习新的、更有效的管理冲突的方式来改变它。

transcript.text: When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account.
transcript.translation: 当你卷入冲突时，有两个主要考虑因素你需要考虑。

transcript.text: Achieving your personal goals, and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
transcript.translation: 实现你的个人目标，并保持与对方的良好关系。

transcript.text: How important your personal goals are, and how important the relationship is to you, affect how you act in a conflict.
transcript.translation: 你的个人目标有多重要，以及关系对你有多重要，影响你在冲突中的行为方式。

transcript.text: Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
transcript.translation: 鉴于这两个考虑因素，可以识别出五种管理冲突的风格。

transcript.text: The Turtle.
transcript.translation: 乌龟型。

transcript.text: Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
transcript.translation: 乌龟缩进壳里以避免冲突。

transcript.text: They give up their personal goals and relationships.
transcript.translation: 他们放弃个人目标和关系。

transcript.text: They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
transcript.translation: 他们认为从冲突中撤退比面对它更容易。

transcript.text: The Shark.
transcript.translation: 鲨鱼型。

transcript.text: Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
transcript.translation: 鲨鱼试图通过强迫对手接受他们对冲突的解决方案来压倒对手。

transcript.text: They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
transcript.translation: 他们不惜一切代价寻求实现目标。

transcript.text: Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
transcript.translation: 鲨鱼认为冲突的解决是一方赢一方输。

transcript.text: Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
transcript.translation: 胜利给鲨鱼带来自豪感和成就感。

transcript.text: Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
transcript.translation: 失败给他们带来软弱、不足和失败感。

transcript.text: The Teddy Bear.
transcript.translation: 泰迪熊型。

transcript.text: Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
transcript.translation: 泰迪熊希望被他人接受和喜爱。

transcript.text: They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
transcript.translation: 他们认为应该为了和谐而避免冲突，并且相信讨论冲突无法不损害关系。

transcript.text: They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
transcript.translation: 他们放弃目标以维护关系。

transcript.text: The Fox.
transcript.translation: 狐狸型。

transcript.text: Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
transcript.translation: 狐狸对自己的目标以及与他人的关系有适度的关注。

transcript.text: They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
transcript.translation: 他们放弃部分目标，并说服冲突中的对方放弃部分目标。

transcript.text: They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
transcript.translation: 他们寻求冲突的解决方案，让双方都能获得一些东西。

transcript.text: The Owl.
transcript.translation: 猫头鹰型。

transcript.text: Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
transcript.translation: 猫头鹰将冲突视为需要解决的问题。

transcript.text: They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
transcript.translation: 他们认为冲突通过减少两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。

transcript.text: They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
transcript.translation: 他们试图开始一场将冲突识别为问题的讨论。

transcript.text: By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
transcript.translation: 通过寻求满足自己和对方的解决方案，猫头鹰维护了关系。

transcript.text: Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
transcript.translation: 猫头鹰只有在找到实现自己目标和对方目标的解决方案时才满意，并且只有在紧张和负面情绪完全解决时才满意。

transcript.translation: 问题16到18基于你刚刚听到的讲座。

transcript.text: Question 16. Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?
transcript.translation: 问题16. 为什么演讲者说管理冲突的策略总是可以改变的？

transcript.text: Question 17. What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?
transcript.translation: 问题17. 据说什么影响了一个人在冲突中的行为方式？

transcript.text: Question 18. Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?
transcript.translation: 问题18. 在演讲者讨论的五种风格中，哪一种将冲突视为需要解决的问题？

options.label: A
options.text: The fox.

options.label: B
options.text: The owl.

options.label: C

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音2。

transcript.text: The genetic code of all 1.
transcript.translation: 所有1.的基因编码。

transcript.text: 5 million known species of animals and plants living on Earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.
transcript.translation: 地球上所有已知的5百万动植物物种的基因编码将被绘制，以帮助拯救物种免于灭绝并促进人类健康。

transcript.text: Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops and agriculture, and create new biomaterials.
transcript.translation: 科学家们希望，破解动植物的基因编码有助于发现新的传染病治疗方法、延缓衰老、改进作物和农业，并创造新的生物材料。

transcript.text: In Britain, organisations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants.
transcript.translation: 在英国，包括自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和Wellcome Sanger研究所在内的组织已联手对英国66,000种动植物进行基因测序。

transcript.text: Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million.
transcript.translation: 该项目被称为达尔文生命之树项目，预计耗时10年，耗资1亿英镑。

transcript.text: Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
transcript.translation: 一旦完成，所有信息将对研究人员公开可用。

transcript.text: Many scientists believe that Earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500.
transcript.translation: 许多科学家认为，地球现已进入第六次大规模灭绝，人类造成的栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的有害混合，已导致自1500年以来至少77种哺乳动物和140种鸟类的灭绝。

transcript.text: It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago.
transcript.translation: 这是自6600万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大的物种损失。

transcript.text: Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionise the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
transcript.translation: 科学家们表示，对每个物种进行测序将彻底改变对生物学和进化的理解，加强保护以及保护和恢复生物多样性的努力。

transcript.text: Dr Tim Littlewood, Head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum said, Whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic make-up.
transcript.translation: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部主任Tim Littlewood博士说：“无论你对食物还是疾病感兴趣，地球上每个生物体如何适应其环境的历史都记录在其基因组成中。”

transcript.text: How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it.
transcript.translation: 你如何利用这一点取决于你理解它的能力。

transcript.text: We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past.
transcript.translation: 我们将使用现代方法来获得对现在和过去的真正良好窗口。

transcript.text: And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future.
transcript.translation: 当然，对过去的窗口为你提供了未来的前瞻模型。

transcript.text: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome said, Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project.
transcript.translation: Wellcome科学总监Jim Smith爵士说：“尽我所能，我无法想到一个更令人兴奋、更相关、更及时或更具国际启发性的项目。”

transcript.text: Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60% of animal populations.
transcript.translation: 自1970年以来，人类已消灭了60%的动物种群。

transcript.text: About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction.
transcript.translation: 在调查的80,000个物种中，约有23,000个正接近灭绝。

transcript.text: We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply.
transcript.translation: 我们正处于地球上生命的第六次大灭绝事件之中，这不仅威胁着野生动物物种，也危及全球粮食供应。

transcript.text: As scientists, we all realise we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now.
transcript.translation: 作为科学家，我们都意识到我们现在迫切需要对我们脆弱星球上的生命进行编目。

transcript.text: I think we're making history.
transcript.translation: 我认为我们正在创造历史。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音3。

transcript.text: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century No man is an island entire of itself.
transcript.translation: 英国诗人约翰·邓恩在17世纪写道：没有人是一座孤岛。

transcript.text: Every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.
transcript.translation: 每个人都是大陆的一片，是整体的一部分。

transcript.text: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical and cultural level than people realise.
transcript.translation: 如今，一位英国学者声称，人类个体性确实只是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、身体和文化层面的互联程度远超人们的认知。

transcript.text: In his new book, The Self-Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as self and not even our bodies are truly us.
transcript.translation: 在他的新书《自我错觉》中，雷丁大学生态与进化研究组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授认为，根本不存在所谓的自我，甚至我们的身体也不是真正的我们。

transcript.text: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity.
transcript.translation: 正如哥白尼意识到地球不是宇宙的中心一样，奥利弗教授表示，社会迫切需要一场类似哥白尼式的革命，以理解人们不是孤立的存在，而是一个相互联系的身份的一部分。

transcript.text: A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution, he writes.
transcript.translation: 他写道，人类心智文化进化中的一个重要里程碑是接受地球不是宇宙的中心，即所谓的哥白尼革命。

transcript.text: However, we have one more big myth to dispose of, that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe.
transcript.translation: 然而，我们还有一个更大的迷思需要破除，即我们作为独立自我存在于主观宇宙的中心。

transcript.text: You may feel as if you are an independent individual acting autonomously in the world, that you have unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor point with the world changing around you.
transcript.translation: 你可能感觉自己是一个独立个体，在世界中自主行动，拥有一个贯穿一生的不变内在自我，作为世界的中心锚点，而世界在你周围变化。

transcript.text: This is the illusion I seek to tackle.
transcript.translation: 这正是我试图解决的幻觉。

transcript.text: We are intimately connected to the world around us.
transcript.translation: 我们与周围的世界紧密相连。

transcript.text: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material us is constantly changing.
transcript.translation: 奥利弗教授认为，人体内大约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物质上的我们是不断变化的。

transcript.text: In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years.
transcript.translation: 事实上，你身体中没有任何部分存在超过10年。

transcript.text: Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient.
transcript.translation: 既然我们的身体基本上每隔几周就会重新生成，那么仅凭其中的物质显然是不够的。

transcript.text: To explain the persistent thread of an identity, Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society and only by realizing we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.
transcript.translation: 为了解释身份持续性的线索，奥利弗教授声称，个人主义实际上对社会有害，只有意识到我们是一个更大实体的一部分，才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。

transcript.text: Through selfish overconsumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate.
transcript.translation: 通过自私的过度消费，我们正在破坏自然世界，并以加速的速度消耗不可再生资源。

transcript.text: We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behavior to act in less selfish ways, he said.

questionGroups.title: The Curious Case of the Tree That Owns Itself

material.title: The Curious Case of the Tree That Owns Itself

paragraphs.text: In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark—a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world. So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?
paragraphs.translation: 在乔治亚州雅典市，有一个相当奇特的当地地标——一棵大白橡树，几乎普遍被认为它拥有自己。因此，它被认为是世界上最著名的树木之一。那么，这棵树是如何拥有自己和周围土地的呢？

paragraphs.text: Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. It states, "Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human. Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it."
paragraphs.translation: 据报道，在19世纪的某个时候，一位名叫威廉·杰克逊上校的乔治亚人喜欢上了这棵树，并努力保护它免受任何危险。至于他为何如此喜爱它，最早记载这个故事的是1890年8月12日发表在《雅典每周旗帜报》上的一篇匿名头版文章。文章写道：“杰克逊上校从小就看着这棵树长大，几乎像爱一个人一样爱上了它。它茂盛的树叶和坚实的枝干经常为他遮挡大雨，他多次从它最高的树枝上取下鸣禽的蛋。他看着它成长，当到了晚年，看到这棵树以宏伟的姿态屹立时，他痛心地想到，自己死后它可能会落入那些可能摧毁它的人手中。”

paragraphs.text: Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. The deed read, "W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides."
paragraphs.translation: 为此，杰克逊通过契约将这棵树及其周围一小块土地的所有权转让给了树本身。契约写道：“W. H. 杰克逊，出于他对所述树木的深厚感情以及他希望看到它受到保护的强烈愿望，将所述橡树的完全占有权以及其周围八英尺内所有土地转让给了它。”

paragraphs.text: In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians (看管者) of Earth. Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.
paragraphs.translation: 久而久之，这棵树成为一个旅游景点，被称为“拥有自己的树”。然而，在20世纪初，这棵树开始显示出缓慢死亡的迹象，几乎无能为力。时间之父最终会降临到我们所有人身上，即使是我们通常长寿、高大、枝叶茂盛的地球同胞看管者。最后，在1942年10月9日，这棵超过30米高、树龄200-400年的树倒了，据传闻是由于一场强风暴和/或先前已死亡且根部腐烂所致。

paragraphs.text: About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree. And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.
paragraphs.translation: 大约四年后，初级女子园艺俱乐部的成员（在树不幸死亡前曾照料它）追踪到一棵从原始树上取下的坚果长成的小树。于是，在1946年10月9日，在乔治亚大学农学院罗伊·鲍登教授的指导下，这棵小树被移植到其祖先的位置。几个月后，举行了一场官方仪式，出席的正是雅典市长罗伯特·L·麦克沃特，以纪念这一时刻。

paragraphs.text: This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.
paragraphs.translation: 这棵新树被称为“拥有自己的树的儿子”，并被假设为原始树的继承人，自然继承了它所站立的土地。当然，已知有数十棵其他树木从原始树繁衍而来，因为人们从它那里取坚果在其他地方种植是必然的。尽管如此，迄今为止，原始树的其他后代都没有向法院申请他们的土地份额，所以似乎一切都好。无论如何，“拥有自己的树的儿子”至今仍然屹立，尽管通常简称为“拥有自己的树”。

paragraphs.text: This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.
paragraphs.translation: 这一切让我们回到杰克逊最初是否真的将树的合法所有权授予树本身，以及这样的契约是否具有法律约束力。

paragraphs.text: Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.
paragraphs.translation: 首先，事实证明杰克逊只在雅典度过了大约三年时间，从43岁开始，从1829年到1832年，这在一定程度上否定了他小时候在树下度过时光、看着它长大然后担心它死后会发生什么的想法。此外，对雅典土地所有权记录的广泛搜索似乎并未表明杰克逊曾拥有树所在的土地。

paragraphs.text: He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear. Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31,000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.
paragraphs.translation: 在那三年里，他确实住在紧挨着它的一块土地上，但是否拥有那块土地并不清楚。无论如何，在1832年，一块四英亩的土地，包括树所在的土地和杰克逊居住的邻近土地等，被卖给了大学教授马尔萨斯·A·沃德。在交易中，沃德需要向杰克逊支付1200美元（约合今天的31,000美元），无论是为了财产本身还是仅仅作为杰克逊在地块上所做改进的补偿。最终，无论他是否拥有邻近地块，还是仅仅被允许在他在大学工作期间使用它，他肯定从未拥有树生长的地块，这是当前话题最重要的一点。

paragraphs.text: After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.
paragraphs.translation: 在沃德教授购买土地后，杰克逊和他的家人在几英里外购买了一块655英亩的土地并搬到了那里。十年后，1844年，杰克逊似乎遇到了财务困难，他的小种植园被克拉克县治安官办公室查封并拍卖以清偿抵押贷款。因此，如果他拥有雅典本身的一些土地，包括树所在的土地，他可能会卖掉它来筹集资金，或者也会被拿走。

paragraphs.text: And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.
paragraphs.translation: 无论情况如何，杰克逊应该知道需要为契约土地支付财产税，以确保树的未来真正安全。然而，没有任何账目或记录表明为此设立了任何信托或类似机构。

paragraphs.text: On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.
paragraphs.translation: 除此之外，没有确凿证据表明这样的契约曾经存在过，尽管雅典的契约记录可以追溯到杰克逊1876年去世前几十年，并且根据最初声称见过它的匿名新闻记者，它应该在1890年的档案中存在。

paragraphs.text: As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?
paragraphs.translation: 正如你从这一切中可能想象的那样，很少有人相信故事的这一面。那么，这一切是如何发生的呢？

paragraphs.text: It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled "Deeded to Itself", which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.
paragraphs.translation: 据推测，它是由前述1890年头版文章《转让给自己》中匿名作者的想象力虚构的，顺便说一句，这篇文章包含几个更容易被证明是虚假的元素。至于作者为何这样做，据推测，这或许是19世纪版本的点击诱饵思维练习，探讨某人是否合法地将这样一个无意识的生物转让给自己。

paragraphs.text: Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.
paragraphs.translation: 无论如何，下一次提到“拥有自己的树”的已知实例直到1901年才出现在同一份报纸《雅典每周旗帜报》的百年纪念版上。这期报纸刊登了另一篇报道，很明显只是复制了大约十年前发表的原文，只是稍微改写了一下。下一次报道是在1906年，再次在《雅典每周旗帜报》上，再次很明显地复制了原始报道，只是稍微改写，相当于19世纪当观众已经忘记原文时的重新发布。

questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself'（杰克逊通过契约将树本身及其周围一小片土地的所有权转让给了树），与陈述中的'Jackson was said to have transferred his ownership of the oak tree to itself in order to protect it from being destroyed'（据说杰克逊将自己的橡树所有权转让给了树本身，以保护它免遭破坏）相对应。关键词匹配：ownership of the oak tree对应ownership of the tree, protect it from being destroyed对应to protect it。

questions.statementText: No proof has been found from an extensive search that Jackson had ever owned the land where the oak tree grew.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落H。段落H中提到'an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on'（在雅典进行的广泛的土地所有权记录搜索似乎没有显示杰克逊曾经拥有过树所在的土地），与陈述中的'No proof has been found from an extensive search that Jackson had ever owned the land where the oak tree grew'（从广泛的搜索中没有找到证据表明杰克逊曾经拥有过橡树生长的土地）相对应。关键词匹配：extensive search对应extensive search, owned the land对应owned the land。

questions.statementText: When it was raining heavily, Jackson often took shelter under a big tree that is said to own itself.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落B。段落B中提到'Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains'（它的茂密树叶和坚固的枝条经常保护他免受大雨侵袭），与陈述中的'When it was raining heavily, Jackson often took shelter under a big tree that is said to own itself'（当雨下得很大时，杰克逊经常在一棵据说拥有自己的大树下避难）相对应。关键词匹配：protected him from the heavy rains对应took shelter under a big tree, heavy rains对应raining heavily。

questions.statementText: There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes for the land on which the oak tree sat.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落K。段落K中提到'Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this'（然而没有任何账目或记录表明设立了任何信托或类似机构来促进这一点），与陈述中的'There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes for the land on which the oak tree sat'（没有证据表明杰克逊已经安排支付橡树所在土地的财产税）相对应。关键词匹配：no account or record indicates对应no evidence, pay property taxes对应pay property taxes。

questions.statementText: Professor Ward paid Jackson over one thousand dollars when purchasing a piece of land from him.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落I。段落I中提到'In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200'（在交易中，沃德被要求支付给杰克逊1200美元），与陈述中的'Professor Ward paid Jackson over one thousand dollars when purchasing a piece of land from him'（沃德教授在购买他的一块土地时支付给杰克逊超过一千元）相对应。关键词匹配：paid Jackson a sum of $1,200对应paid Jackson over one thousand dollars, purchasing a piece of land对应purchasing a piece of land。

questions.statementText: It is said the tree that owned itself fell in a heavy windstorm.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落D。段落D中提到'the tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm'（有传言说，树倒下是因为一场严重的风暴），与陈述中的'It is said the tree that owned itself fell in a heavy windstorm'（据说拥有自己的树在一场大风中倒下）相对应。关键词匹配：fell in a severe windstorm对应fell in a heavy windstorm。

questions.statementText: The story of the oak tree is suspected to have been invented as a thought exercise.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落N。段落N中提到'it is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author'（人们推测这是由上述匿名作者的想象所发明的），与陈述中的'The story of the oak tree is suspected to have been invented as a thought exercise'（橡树的故事被怀疑是作为思维练习而发明的）相对应。关键词匹配：invented by the imagination对应suspected to have been invented, thought exercise对应thought exercise。

questions.statementText: Jackson's little plantation was auctioned off to settle his debt in the mid-19th century.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落J。段落J中提到'in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage'（在1844年，杰克逊似乎遇到了财务困难，他的小种植园被克拉克县警长办公室扣押并拍卖以清偿抵押贷款），与陈述中的'Jackson's little plantation was auctioned off to settle his debt in the mid-19th century'（杰克逊的小种植园在19世纪中叶被拍卖以清偿他的债务）相对应。关键词匹配：auctioned off to settle the mortgage对应auctioned off to settle his debt, mid-19th century对应1844。

questions.statementText: An official ceremony was held to celebrate the transplanting of a small tree to where its ancestor had stood.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落E。段落E中提到'And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion'（于是在1946年10月9日，在佐治亚大学农业学院的Roy Bowden教授的指导下，这棵小树被移植到了它祖先的位置。几个月后，举行了一个官方仪式，由雅典市长Robert L McWhorter主持，以纪念这一时刻），与陈述中的'An official ceremony was held to celebrate the transplanting of a small tree to where its ancestor had stood'（举行了一个官方仪式，庆祝一棵小树被移植到其祖先曾经站立的地方）相对应。关键词匹配：an official ceremony was held对应an official ceremony was held, transplanting of a small tree to where its ancestor had stood对应transplanted to the location of its ancestor。

questions.statementText: The story of the Tree That Owns Itself appeared in the local paper several times, with slight alterations in wording.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落O。段落O中提到'the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded'（下一次已知的提到拥有自己的树的情况是在1901年，同样是在雅典周报的百年版上。这篇文章非常清楚地只是复制了大约十年前发表的原始文章，只是稍微改写了一些词。下一次报道是在1906年，再次在雅典周报上，再次非常清楚地复制了原始报道，只是稍微改写了一些词），与陈述中的'The story of the Tree That Owns Itself appeared in the local paper several times, with slight alterations in wording'（拥有自己的树的故事在当地报纸上出现了几次，措辞略有改动）相对应。关键词匹配：appeared in the local paper several times对应appeared in the local paper, slight alterations in wording对应slight alterations in wording。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?
paragraphs.translation: 员工知道对错，这是无可辩驳的。那么，为什么当他们在工作中看到有人表现出高风险行为时，更多的员工不进行干预呢？

paragraphs.text: There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.
paragraphs.translation: 有许多因素影响人们是否进行干预。首先，他们需要能够看到风险情况开始出现。其次，公司的文化需要让他们感到安全，敢于发声。第三，他们需要具备有效沟通的技巧来表达意见。

paragraphs.text: This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect—the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
paragraphs.translation: 这不仅仅是工作场所的问题；它也是一个日益增长的非工作场所问题。每天人们在街上目睹事件，却选择袖手旁观。这被称为旁观者效应——目睹事件的人越多，该群体中任何人帮助受害者的可能性就越小。这背后的心理学叫做责任扩散。基本上，人群越大，越多的人认为别人会处理——意味着在需要时刻没有人有效地干预或行动。

paragraphs.text: This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.
paragraphs.translation: 这种从众心理强大到足以让人们逃避他们已知的责任。但在工作场所，不仅仅是前线员工不进行安全干预。也有主管不干预的情况。

paragraphs.text: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
paragraphs.translation: 当一群员工看到不安全行为没有在领导层面得到处理时，这就创造了一个先例，即这种情况应该如何处理，从而为所有人定义了安全文化。

paragraphs.text: Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管鼓励工人在观察到不安全操作时进行干预，但这种情况发生不到一半。恐惧是导致不干预的最终因素。有对惩罚的恐惧，有担心干预后需要做更多工作的恐惧。过去的失败尝试是另一个导致人们不干预的重要因素——他们倾向于在未来所有情况下将这一行动推给别人。

paragraphs.text: On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger.
paragraphs.translation: 在许多工作场所，必须指定有能力的工人。他们的部分职责是在工人没有使用适当设备或条件不安全时进行干预。有能力的工人还需要在存在危险时停止工作继续进行。

paragraphs.text: Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
paragraphs.translation: 主管也扮演着关键角色。即使不需要有能力的人员，主管也需要一系列广泛的技能，不仅要识别和减轻工作场所危害，还要在他们的团队内建立支持干预和开放沟通的安全氛围。

paragraphs.text: Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.
paragraphs.translation: 除了有能力的工人和主管之外，重要的是教育组织内的每个人，无论你是被指定的有能力的人员、主管还是前线员工，如果你目睹可能的不安全行为，都有义务进行干预。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
paragraphs.translation: 术语“环保主义者”可以意味着不同的事情。它过去指的是试图保护野生动物和自然生态系统的人。在21世纪，该术语已经演变，以涵盖对抗人为气候变化的必要性。

paragraphs.text: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
paragraphs.translation: 这两种环保主义分支之间的区别是科学界内部关于核能分裂的原因。

paragraphs.text: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
paragraphs.translation: 一边是纯粹主义者，他们认为核电不值得冒险，气候危机的唯一解决方案是可再生能源。对立的一方同意可再生能源至关重要，但表示社会需要在没有阳光和风力时，仍有足够的电力来满足消费者的基本需求。核能比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多，是一个自然的选择，尤其是在水电能力有限的地方。

paragraphs.text: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
paragraphs.translation: Leon Clarke，曾帮助撰写联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会的报告，他并不是核能的盲目支持者，但表示如果我们认真对待实现碳中和，核能是一个有价值的选择。

paragraphs.text: "Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."
paragraphs.translation: “这一切的核心在于你认为我们能在多大程度上通过100%的可再生能源实现气候目标，”他说。“如果你不相信我们能做到，而你关心气候，你就不得不考虑像核能这样的东西。”

paragraphs.text: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
paragraphs.translation: 普遍实现100%可再生能源的可行性同样存在争议。像佛蒙特州伯灵顿这样的城市，多年来一直是“100%可再生能源”。但这些城市通常人口较少，偶尔仍依赖化石燃料能源，并且拥有直接可用的丰富可再生资源。与此同时，那些能够依靠可再生能源运行的国家，通常是因为拥有非凡的水电能力。

paragraphs.text: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.
paragraphs.translation: 德国是大型工业化国家推动绿色能源的最佳案例研究。总理安格拉·默克尔在2011年宣布了Energiewende，这是一项能源转型计划，将逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时引入可再生能源。自2010年以来，风能和太阳能发电增长了400%以上，2019年可再生能源提供了该国46%的电力。

paragraphs.text: But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
paragraphs.translation: 但近年来进展已经停滞。可再生能源的不稳定性不仅意味着夜间往往无法发电，还意味着太阳能和风能在白天可能压倒电网，迫使公用事业公司付费给客户来使用他们的电力。落后的电网基础设施难以将这种过剩的绿色能源从德国北部运往工业南部，这意味着许多工厂仍然依靠煤炭和天然气运行。在一些地方，政治极限也已达到，公民对新建风力涡轮机表示强烈抗议。

paragraphs.text: The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
paragraphs.translation: 结果是，德国的温室气体排放自2010年以来下降了约11.5%——低于欧盟13.5%的平均水平。

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第三段提到'Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited'，表明反对者提出在必要时选择核能作为解决方案，因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively'是纯化论者的观点，不是反对者的观点
wrongOptions.B: 'Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately'与文章内容不符
wrongOptions.D: 'Limiting people's non-basic consumption'在文章中未提及

questions.questionText: What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example?

options.label: A
options.text: It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world's exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable.

options.label: B
options.text: It is contentious whether cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal.

options.label: C
options.text: It is arguable whether cities that manage to run off renewables have sustainable hydroelectric capabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: It is debatable whether traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章第五段提到'The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious'，并通过Burlington的例子说明即使是小城市也难以完全依赖可再生能源，暗示全球范围内实现100%可再生能源的争议性，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'Cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal'与Burlington的例子无关
wrongOptions.C: 'Cities that manage to run off renewables have sustainable hydroelectric capabilities'与Burlington的例子无关
wrongOptions.D: 'Traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world'与Burlington的例子无关

questions.questionText: What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy?

options.label: A
options.text: It has increased its wind and solar power generation four times over the last two decades.

options.label: B
options.text: It represents a good example of a major industrialized country promoting green energy.

options.label: C
options.text: It relies on renewable energy to generate more than half of its electricity.

options.label: D
options.text: It has succeeded in reaching the goal of energy transition set by Merkel.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章最后一段提到'Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy'，表明德国是推动绿色能源的大型工业化国家的典范，因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010'虽然正确，但不是德国在可再生能源方面的全部情况
wrongOptions.C: 'renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019'，说明德国并未超过一半的电力来自可再生能源
wrongOptions.D: 'Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010'说明德国在能源转型方面并未完全成功

questions.questionText: What may be one of the reasons for Germany's progress having halted in recent years?

options.label: A
options.text: Its grid infrastructure's capacity has fallen behind its development of green energy.

options.label: B
options.text: Its overabundance of green energy has forced power plants to suspend operation during daytime.

options.label: C
options.text: Its industrial south is used to running factories on conventional energy supplies.

options.label: D
options.text: Its renewable energy supplies are unstable both at night and during the day.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章倒数第二段提到'Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south'，表明电网基础设施的落后是德国近年来进展停滞的原因之一，因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'Overabundance of green energy has forced power plants to suspend operation during daytime'与文章内容不符
wrongOptions.C: 'Its industrial south is used to running factories on conventional energy supplies'在文章中未提及
wrongOptions.D: 'Its renewable energy supplies are unstable both at night and during the day'虽然提到了可再生能源的不稳定性，但不是进展停滞的唯一原因

questionGroups.sourceText: 中国的传统婚礼习俗历史悠久，从周朝开始就逐渐形成了一套完整的婚礼仪式，有些一直沿用至今。如今的中式婚礼习俗已有很大变化，但婚礼庆典仍然十分隆重。婚礼场地经过精心装饰，以象征喜庆（jubilance）的红色为主色调，摆放着许多祝愿新人幸福的物件。在婚礼上，新人要拜天地（bow to Heaven and Earth），拜父母和相互对拜，然后设宴招待宾客，并向宾客敬酒致谢。今天，许多年轻人依然钟情于传统的中式婚礼，体验独特而美好的中国式浪漫。

answer.modelTranslation: China's traditional wedding customs have a long history, gradually forming a complete set of wedding ceremonies since the Zhou Dynasty, some of which are still in use today. Modern Chinese wedding customs have changed significantly, but the wedding celebrations remain very grand. The wedding venue is meticulously decorated, with the color red, symbolizing jubilance, as the main theme, and many objects are placed to wish the newlyweds happiness. At the wedding, the couple bow to Heaven and Earth, bow to their parents and each other, then hold a banquet to entertain guests and toast to thank them. Today, many young people still have a fondness for traditional Chinese weddings, experiencing a unique and beautiful Chinese romance.
